name: Portland, OR
subtitle: Food cart capital — from Le Pigeon to Voodoo
items: Le Pigeon (Gabriel Rucker, lower Burnside — James Beard winner)
Pok Pok (Andy Ricker, Thai — the SE Asian chicken wings that changed everything)
Tasty n Daughters (NW, brunch — the fried chicken sandwich)
Ox (NE, Argentine wood-fired, daily changing menu)
Toro Bravo (John Gorham, NE, Spanish — iconic tapas bar)
Ava Gene's (Division, vegetable-forward Italian, serious contender)
Apizza Scholls (Division, New Haven-style — possibly Oregon's best pizza)
Jake's Famous Crawfish (SW, since 1892 — Portland's oldest seafood)
Kenny & Zuke's Delicatessen (Alder, NYC-style deli in the Pacific NW)
Screen Door (NE, Southern cooking — the line is not a myth)
Pine State Biscuits (multiple, biscuits & gravy + fried chicken)
Nostrana (SE, wood-fired pizza + Italian)
Luce (Division, Italian wine bar + pasta)
Nong's Khao Man Gai (cart → restaurant, Thai rice + chicken — a legend)
Bollywood Theater (Division + NE, Indian street food done right)
Canard (Williams, Gabriel Rucker's bar — snacks + wine)
Mucca Osteria (SE, Italian neighborhood gem)
Han Oak (NE, Korean — Peter Cho, James Beard nominee)
Voodoo Doughnut (Old Town — the cultural institution)
Portland Saturday Market + Food Carts (SW 10th & Alder)
